messages:
From: Michael Lane <michael.lane@telecomco.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Offline deployment — courier escrow & signing cadence

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the call earlier. We're standing up our first off-network rollout for the closed racks and need to lock down the operational cadence for courier escrow, signer rotation, and activation windows. A few specific questions we didn't get to: 

1) How often should we rotate the on-site operator signer keys for a regular monthly delivery vs. an emergency hotfix?
2) Do you support a threshold signing model (t-of-n) for curator approvals, or is it a single HSM-backed signing key per site?
3) What's the minimum manifest metadata Redwood requires for push acceptance (hashes, build-id, operator-id, timestamp)?

We also want to make sure chain-of-custody attachments and proof-of-origin are compatible with our courier's proof-of-delivery system. If you can share a sample manifest and a checklist we can give to the field ops team, that would help.

Attached: none on our side — can accept your sample docs.

Thanks,
Michael
Senior Infrastructure Manager — TelecomCo

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Michael Lane <michael.lane@telecomco.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Offline deployment — courier escrow & signing cadence

Michael — thanks for the clear list. Short answers first, then proposed operational playbook below.

1) Rotation cadence: monthly for standard deliveries; immediate rotation after any unexpected access event or signatory loss. For emergency hotfixes we recommend one-time ephemeral signing keys with audit-backed expiration (24–72 hours) and return-to-root rotation within 24 hours of activation.

2) We support both models. Recommended default: HSM-backed site key with an upstream threshold signature for higher-risk environments (2-of-3 operator quorum). Threshold signing reduces single-operator blast radius and gives a clean audit trail.

3) Minimum manifest fields: build_id, artifact_hash (sha256), image_size_bytes, origin_repo, signer_id(s), signature_scheme, timestamp_utc, activation_window (start/end), operator_contact, operator_id_roster_ref. See attached manifest-sample.json.

Proposed playbook (high-level):
- Pre-delivery: customer and courier sign an escrow agreement + manifest generated and signed by Redwood staging HSM.
- Courier handoff: manifest + sealed media transferred to courier; courier records POD with GPS/time and signed receipt.
- On-site: operator(s) perform key ceremony, verify manifest hashes, and perform local signing (site HSM) if policy requires. Activation window enforced by on-site operator and remote acceptance webhook (optional).
- Post-activation: automatic upload of activation proof (signed receipt + operator signature) to our audit ledger.

I've attached three documents: offline-escrow-checklist.xlsx (delivery checklist), signer-roster.csv (initial operator roster template), manifest-sample.json (manifest schema). Jonas and Karthik—please review the signer rotation parameters and the HSM workflow; I've flagged two decisions we need from Security.

Thanks,
Sofia
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: offline-escrow-checklist.xlsx, signer-roster.csv, manifest-sample.json

Team — quick technical follow-up and a couple of edits for the attachments.

Notes: 
- For threshold signing we should call out the supported schemes: FROST-based threshold ECDSA or a pre-signed K-of-N envelope approach. Operationally, FROST is cleaner for distributed operators but requires client-side libs; envelope signing is simpler for legacy operator tooling.
- Signer rotation: recommend staggered rotation schedule so not all operator keys rotate at once — e.g., rotation window spread over 3 days with overlap for continuity.
- Manifest: add a "provenance_chain" array to capture upstream build artifacts (container layer digests + repo commit ids). This helps when customers want reproducible audits.

Attached updated manifest-sample.json (v2) and a short change log. Also flagged the escrow checklist to add a courier contact section and a failover courier procedure.

Action items for Security: confirm whether Redwood CI will publish a long-term signing key anchor or if each build will be signed by ephemeral CI keys and then counter-signed by our root HSM.

Jonas
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: manifest-sample.json (v2), manifest-changelog.txt

Michael — following up with the finalized playbook and next steps. We've incorporated Jonas's v2 manifest and added the courier failover section. Summary and owners below: 

Decisions and owners:
- Signing model: default HSM site key + optional 2-of-3 FROST threshold for high-risk sites (Owner: Sofia).
- Rotation cadence: monthly rolling rotation (3-day stagger), immediate rotation on incident (Owner: Operations — Karthik).
- Manifest schema: use manifest-sample.json v2; add provenance_chain and activation_proof fields (Owner: Jonas).
- Courier escrow: add courier P.O.D. with GPS/PIN + signed courier receipt (Owner: TelecomCo operations).

Next steps / deadlines:
- TelecomCo to confirm preferred threshold model by 2028-05-24 (Michael).
- Redwood to publish final manifest v2 + checklist to shared drive and open JIRA SECOPS-4217 for Security confirmation by 2028-05-22 (Sofia/Jonas).
- Field ops rehearsal: schedule a dry-run handoff with TelecomCo courier week of 2028-06-04 (Karthik coordinating).

I've uploaded final docs to the Drive folder and linked the JIRA ticket above. If TelecomCo wants an on-site or remote walkthrough of the key ceremony we can schedule a 90-minute workshop during the rehearsal week.

Thanks all — this is a good incremental design that keeps risk low while giving TelecomCo the auditability they need.

Best,
Sofia
